## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
No trials yet. The starting net scored 0, which fits what earlier searches saw: unhedged nets score 0 when the world deviates from its description. Nothing is ruled out yet. One thing can be said without data. The obs enters through a 1x1 conv, which treats every input channel alike, so a pure reordering of obs channels cannot by itself explain a zero. Because of that, no candidate spends its slot on channel order. This round includes the required reference net and five layout hedges, all on the reference recipe: (1) 16 mask and output layouts (8 grid symmetries × type-major/type-minor order); (2) a 5x5 head conv for other footprints and anchors; (3) a second path with DONE at index 0; (4) the obs under all grid symmetries, in case it is transposed or flipped relative to the mask; (5) all of these combined, to find out whether any deviation can be escaped at all. If n_place ≠ n_types·Y·X, every file falls back to a Linear mask embedding and a Linear output.

### Round 2
All 6 round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 in training. Ruled out as the sole deviation, assuming the hedged net can learn it: an action layout among the 8 grid symmetries times type-major/type-minor order; DONE at index 0; the obs flipped or transposed relative to the mask (r1c5 concatenates all 8 obs symmetries, so the 1x1 stem could even realign build and target channels separately); footprint or anchor shifts within ±2 cells. Obs channel order is already learnable by the 1x1 stem. Five deviations are still open: (a) obs memory read in the wrong order, e.g. channel-last data presented as [C,Y,X]; (b) an arbitrary action-index or obs permutation, or a different action count; (c) a global spatial offset or wrap between groups that local convs cannot reach; (d) reward or obs scale that wrecks a shared actor-critic trunk; (e) a stale or lagged build view, so the policy must sequence its moves by episode progress. There is one targeted hedge per deviation, plus one candidate that combines all five.

### Round 3
All 12 trials scored exactly 0 on dev and in training, so there is no signal to follow yet. The results rule out these deviations: action order (16 layouts: 8 grid symmetries × type-first or type-last), the DONE index, anchor or footprint shifts within 2 cells, the whole obs flipped or transposed, a channel-last obs read, reward or obs scale (separate critic with GroupNorm), and a short receptive field (attention). Channel permutations are already covered because the learned 1x1 stem can learn any of them. Hedges not yet tried: (1) the type index in the middle of the action order (Y,T,X) or a different action count, such as compact anchors only where the brick fits, a layer choice (T·Z·Y·X), or another number of types; (2) the target misaligned with the build, so it is rewarded in a different frame from the one shown; (3) a grid that wraps around (torus). I also test all three combined, at the reference recipe and under two long-horizon, higher-entropy recipes. These bet on a reward deviation (sparse shaping or early collapse onto DONE) that gamma 0.9 would hide.

### Round 4
All 18 trials scored exactly 0 on dev and in training, across 3 rounds. The results rule out these deviations: the 16 action/mask layouts (8 grid symmetries times type-major or type-minor order), the 24-layout and compact-anchor factorisations, DONE at index 0, the obs under symmetries or read as channel-last, the target in its own frame, a wrap-around grid, and footprint or anchor shifts within a 5x5 window. Global attention, a separate critic with normalisation, FiLM and dense remaps also failed. Long-horizon and high-entropy recipes failed too. What remains is a learning-prior gap or a dynamics or reward change. No net so far has combined the layout hedge with explicit footprint pooling, which the starting net uses. None has processed the layers explicitly, with a weight-shared per-layer path that can learn other drop rules or heights. Round 4 tests those two and their combinations, including anchors at all four corners and two recipes with more samples.
